Triage one support ticket: read it at its current revision, know who raised it, have a proposed classification reviewed, and route it under authority; escalate under authority when its service-level target is breached, and hand it to a person when it cannot be triaged.

- **Id:** `support.triage`
- **Revision:** 1
- **Source:** [`protocols/support-triage/1.yaml`](https://github.com/beyond10x/engineering-protocols/blob/main/protocols/support-triage/1.yaml)

## Dependency graph

Which actions may produce which evidence, which claims that evidence establishes, and which outcomes and obligations rest on those claims. Hover or focus a node to trace what it rests on.

<ProtocolGraph data={graph} />

## Actions

What can be done in a case: what it needs first, which authority it requires, the class of effect it has and the evidence it may produce.

| Action | Description | Precondition | Requires capability | Effect | May produce |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `classification.review` | approve or reject the proposed classification, under authority | `classification.proposed` is **TRUE** | `classification.review` | `none` | `classification_review` |
| `escalation.request` | request an escalation; needs a current read showing the target breached, and authority | `sla.breached` is **TRUE** | `escalation.request` | `write` | `escalation_record` |
| `reply.draft` | draft a reply to the requester for a person to send; needs the classification decided and authority | `ticket.classified` is **TRUE** | `reply.draft` | `write` | *no evidence* |
| `requester.lookup` | look up the person who raised the ticket | `ticket.current` is **TRUE** | *no authority* | `read` | `requester_profile` |
| `ticket.classify` | propose a category and priority for the ticket; changes nothing outside the case | `ticket.current` is **TRUE** | *no authority* | `none` | `classification` |
| `ticket.read` | read the ticket at its current revision | *none* | *no authority* | `read` | `ticket_snapshot` |
| `ticket.route` | route the ticket to a queue or owner; only after the classification is decided (step order, decision record 0084) and the requester is known, and only under authority | all of (`requester.known` is **TRUE**; `ticket.classified` is **TRUE**) | `ticket.route` | `write` | `routing_record` |

## Evidence kinds

The kinds of evidence this protocol admits. A kind with a maximum age applies for that long after a record's `observed_at`: evaluated at a later instant, the record is excluded as expired.

| Evidence kind | Description | Applies for | Produced by | Used by claims |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `classification` | a proposed category and priority for one ticket revision, each one the deployment declares | *no limit* | `ticket.classify` | `classification.proposed` |
| `classification_review` | a review of the proposed classification; its result is approved or rejected | *no limit* | `classification.review` | `classification.reviewed` |
| `escalation_record` | the record that an escalation was requested for the ticket, naming where it went | *no limit* | `escalation.request` | `escalation.requested` |
| `requester_profile` | the requester looked up; its result is identified or unidentified | *no limit* | `requester.lookup` | `requester.known` |
| `routing_record` | the record that the ticket was routed to a queue or owner, naming the target | *no limit* | `ticket.route` | `ticket.routed` |
| `ticket_snapshot` | the ticket read at one revision: its id, revision, a digest and its service-level status when read, never its text; its result is breached or within\_target. A read older than 15 minutes no longer says whether the target is breached | `15m` after it is observed | `ticket.read` | `sla.breached`, `ticket.current` |

## Claims

Each claim is TRUE, FALSE or UNKNOWN, established from evidence by its predicate. Missing or stale evidence leaves a claim UNKNOWN, never FALSE.

| Claim | Description | True when |
|---|---|---|
| `classification.proposed` | a category and priority are proposed for the current ticket revision | evidence `classification` about `ticket` |
| `classification.reviewed` | the classification of the current ticket revision is reviewed and approved | evidence `classification_review` with result `approved` about `ticket` |
| `escalation.requested` | an escalation is requested for the current ticket revision | evidence `escalation_record` about `ticket` |
| `requester.known` | the requester is identified | evidence `requester_profile` with result `identified` about `requester` |
| `sla.breached` | the ticket's service-level target is breached, by a current read of the ticket | evidence `ticket_snapshot` with result `breached` about `ticket` |
| `ticket.classified` | category and priority are decided on current evidence: the current ticket revision is read, a classification is proposed for it and the review approved it | all of (`classification.proposed` is **TRUE**; `classification.reviewed` is **TRUE**; `ticket.current` is **TRUE**) |
| `ticket.current` | the ticket has been read at its current revision, recently enough to trust | evidence `ticket_snapshot` about `ticket` |
| `ticket.routed` | the current ticket revision is routed to a queue or owner | evidence `routing_record` about `ticket` |
| `ticket.triaged` | category, priority and route are decided on current evidence, for an identified requester | all of (`requester.known` is **TRUE**; `ticket.classified` is **TRUE**; `ticket.routed` is **TRUE**) |

## Obligations

What must be done before a case can be complete, and what discharges it. An obligation stays open until its predicate is TRUE; its predicate being UNKNOWN does not discharge it.

| Obligation | Description | Discharged when |
|---|---|---|
| `escalate_sla_breach` | a breached service-level target needs escalation; discharged once a current read shows the target not breached, or once an escalation is requested | any of (`escalation.requested` is **TRUE**; `sla.breached` is **FALSE**) |

## Outcomes

The legitimate terminal interpretations of a case, and what each requires.

| Outcome | Description | Requires |
|---|---|---|
| `escalated` | the ticket's service-level target is breached and an escalation is requested | all of (`escalation.requested` is **TRUE**; `sla.breached` is **TRUE**) |
| `needs_human` | the ticket goes to a person: the review rejected the proposed classification, or the requester could not be identified | any of (`classification.reviewed` is **FALSE**; `requester.known` is **FALSE**) |
| `triaged` | the ticket is triaged: category, priority and route decided on current evidence, with its service-level target not breached | all of (`sla.breached` is **FALSE**; `ticket.triaged` is **TRUE**) |

## Artifacts

The things whose revisions evidence is bound to.

| Artifact | Description |
|---|---|
| `requester` | the person who raised the ticket, with the organization they belong to |
| `ticket` | the support request a case triages, referenced by its tracker id; its revision moves when the requester's side of the request changes, not when routing fields or internal notes change. The case stores no ticket text |
